children: is facing a major operational incident after a Prime Air cargo aircraft crashed after landing at Miami International Airport on Sunday, killing at least five people and injuring five others.

The Boeing 767-300, operating Flight 7598 from San Juan, Puerto Rico, left the runway and struck vehicles before catching fire. Three injured people were taken to trauma centers in critical condition, while two others received hospital treatment.

Emergency crews deployed about 60 fire apparatus and nearly 200 personnel to manage the wreckage, rescue those trapped and contain a fuel leak. Officials also used specialized teams to address hazards around the aircraft.

The National Transportation Safety Board has started an investigation, while the Federal Aviation Administration will help determine what caused the runway excursion. Amazon said it was working with authorities as more details emerged.
The airport temporarily shut its runways and taxiways, causing flight disruptions before two runways later reopened.
The crash could create near-term uncertainty around Amazon's logistics operations, although the financial impact remains unclear.

title: Amazon Stock in Focus After Cargo Plane Crash Kills 5 in Miami
